solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beast to leave in waste

indicators.note: in tells us the verb for leaving sits inside the word for waste

parts.note: dung is animal waste
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: An animal is told to get out of the muck.
explanation.definitionFit: The dugong is a large marine mammal of the Indian Ocean, a relative of the manatee.

clue.text: Depressed county's attempt to catch fish

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
a cast is a throw of the fishing line

explanation.surface: A depressed county is trying its hand at angling.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast is a synonym for sad or dejected.

clue.text: Beat up group with iron?

parts.note: reads as a violent gang with a weapon, but describes a society of players and the implement such as an iron they use

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means both a society of golfers and an implement like an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a golfers' association and the stick, such as an iron, used to hit the ball.

clue.text: Sweet turned to a gun

indicators.note: turned says the letters of to a gun are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A sweet becomes a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey, nuts and egg white.

clue.text: Moor ship erratically, being unchanged in shape

indicators.note: erratically suggests the letters of moor ship moving about without order

explanation.surface: Someone ties up a vessel badly, though it keeps its form.
explanation.definitionFit: An isomorph is a thing having the same crystalline form or structure as another; 'being' is a noun here, an entity.

clue.text: Beast to stop leaks

definitions.meaning: an earless marine mammal with flippers
to close something tightly so nothing escapes

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a marine mammal and also means to close tight against leakage.

clue.text: Beast in book by Dickens, cut short after a little while

indicators.note: after puts the shortened name later than the brief moment

parts.note: mo, a moment, is a little while
taken as written

indicators.note: cut short says the novelist's name loses its end

parts.note: Charles Dickens, the Victorian novelist

explanation.surface: An animal appears in a Dickens novel, abridged after a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Moby-Dick is the white whale in Herman Melville's novel.

clue.text: Had senior police job and got off

parts.note: had a job running something, ran it
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the detective branch of British police, headed by a senior officer

explanation.surface: Someone held a top police post and was then acquitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got off' suggests escaping a charge; it means went bad, as food does.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off has turned bad or rotten, like rancid butter.

clue.text: Speed has number

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Velocity is a numerical quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: To hasten is to hurry or go faster, a verb sense of speed.

clue.text: Beast forms most of barrier against half a country

indicators.note: most of says the word for barrier loses its final letter

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

indicators.note: half says only the first three of six letters of the country are used

parts.note: Russia is a country

explanation.surface: An animal builds a wall facing a neighbouring state.
explanation.definitionFit: The walrus is a large tusked marine mammal of Arctic seas.

clue.text: Surgeon's maxim on dice

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or maxim
bones is an old slang word for dice

explanation.surface: A surgeon's motto is written on the dice.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Surgeon's is read as 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is a jocular slang term for a surgeon or doctor.

clue.text: Beast of honour or quality

indicators.note: of says the beast is made from letters within the following words

explanation.surface: An animal of noble standing and high calibre.
explanation.definitionFit: The rorqual is a baleen whale of the family that includes the blue whale.

clue.text: Beast seems almost a successful predator

indicators.note: seems almost says the beast's name is nearly what is heard in the phrase

parts.note: a successful predator would catch a lot of prey

explanation.surface: An animal appears to be a very effective hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: The beast's name, said aloud, is close to 'catch a lot', which is what a successful predator does.
explanation.definitionFit: The cachalot is another name for the sperm whale.

clue.text: Counsel these days something gripping?

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
a vice is a tool that grips work

explanation.surface: Someone asks for counsel on something exciting nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel as a noun means guidance or recommendations offered to someone.

clue.text: Wine produced change of air

parts.note: made means produced

indicators.note: change of says the letters of air are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wine brought about a fresh atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of the same name.

clue.text: Five centimes to the pound, in essence

parts.note: a sou was an old French coin worth five centimes
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: Small change adds up, in principle, to a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The soul is the vital essence or core of a person or thing.

clue.text: Heron thus accepts vocal message from duck

indicators.note: accepts says the word for thus takes the duck's call inside it

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: vocal says the duck's call is spelt to match its sound, not its usual spelling

parts.note: a duck's call is a quack

explanation.surface: A heron accepts a duck's spoken greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The squacco is a small buff-coloured heron of southern Europe and Africa.

clue.text: Lines of varied lengths seize up and knock hard

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for seize is read from the bottom

parts.note: to grab is to seize
a rap is a knock
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone grabs and bangs on lines of differing length.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar graph shows data as bars, lines of different lengths.

clue.text: Praise is hesitantly raised and left over

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, says the whole string is read bottom to top

parts.note: to laud is to praise
taken as written
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Praise, given with hesitation, is lifted and abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Residual means remaining, what is left over after the rest has gone.

clue.text: Botanist, no Scot, entertained by early pope

indicators.note: entertained by says the Scots denial is taken inside the pope's name

parts.note: Linus was the second pope, after Peter
nae is Scots for no

explanation.surface: A plant scientist, not Scottish, is hosted by an ancient pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Linnaeus was the Swedish botanist who devised binomial classification of plants and animals.

clue.text: Beast of a chap having a starter

parts.note: a chap is a man
the tee is where a golf hole starts

explanation.surface: An animal belongs to a man who is having a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: The manatee is a large herbivorous aquatic mammal, the sea cow.

clue.text: First part of beast formed tribe in Israel

indicators.note: first part of says only the opening of the monster's name is kept, the rest discarded

parts.note: the leviathan is a biblical sea monster

explanation.surface: A creature's earliest piece made up an ancient Israelite clan.
explanation.walkthrough: The beast is split across two entries: its first part here, its last part at 27 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from Jacob's third son.

clue.text: Beast concealed by flower

parts.note: the orc is a name for the killer whale or grampus
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: An animal is hidden by a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concealed by' looks like a hidden word; 'by' is a link word and ORC is the killer whale.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchid is a showy flowering plant of a large family.

clue.text: Attack causing animal to suffer

parts.note: an ass is an animal
to ail is to suffer illness

explanation.surface: Someone attacks and makes an animal suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, physically or in words.

clue.text: Where to wait for transport in early hour?

indicators.note: in says the vehicle goes inside the time letters

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is early in the day
a bus is transport

explanation.surface: A commuter waits at a bus stop at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bus stop; an ambush is a place where attackers lie in wait.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a hiding place where people lie in wait to attack.

clue.text: Agree to contract again and withdraw

definitions.meaning: to ... is to put one's name to a contract a second time
to give up a post or quit

explanation.definitionFit: Re-sign means sign again, while resign means to quit or step down from a position.

clue.text: Beast dropping American for Scot in hilly region

indicators.note: dropping ... for says one part of the animal's name is swapped out for another

parts.note: the grampus is a dolphin-like cetacean, Risso's dolphin
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: An animal leaves a Yank behind for a Scotsman in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grampians are a mountain range in Scotland; Grampian was also the name of a Scottish region.
explanation.definitionFit: Grampian is the hilly region of north-east Scotland named after its mountains.

clue.text: Last part of beast appearing in comparison

definitions.note: a conjunction used in comparisons, so a phrase describes the word rather than equals it

indicators.note: last part of says only the end of the monster's name is kept

parts.note: the leviathan is a biblical sea monster

explanation.surface: The tail of a monster turns up in a comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: The other part of this beast is at 21 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: This conjunction introduces the second element in a comparison, as in bigger or smaller.

clue.text: Top billing brings man problem

parts.note: the head is the top
AC, account, is a bill
he is a man, by his pronoun

explanation.surface: Getting top billing causes a man trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is a common figure of speech for a troublesome problem or nuisance.

clue.text: Sweet to have a charmed life?

definitions.text: Sweet to have a charmed life?

parts.words: Sweet to have a charmed life?
parts.note: read as a magic charm followed by the verb meaning to exist, which together name a fruit-flavoured sweet

explanation.walkthrough: JUJU is a West African charm and BE means to have life, giving a chewy sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A jujube is a chewy fruit-flavoured lozenge or sweet.

clue.text: Beasts with awfully old steering mechanisms, we hear

indicators.note: awfully says the letters of old are jumbled
we hear says the steering parts are spelt as they sound

parts.note: fins help fish and boats steer

explanation.surface: Animals use badly outdated steering gear, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are small toothed whales, intelligent marine mammals.

clue.text: Beasts in land of dragons, they say

indicators.note: they say indicates the country's name is heard, not seen

parts.note: Wales has a red dragon on its flag

explanation.surface: Animals live in dragon country, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales are the largest marine mammals, the cetaceans.
